Petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India praying that in the
circumstances stated in the affidavit filed therewith, the High Court may be
pleased topleased to issue writ, order or orders specially one in the nature of
Writ of Mandamus declaring the acts of the 4th respondent in calling the
petitioners to police station by making them to sit in the police station without
any crime being registered against the petitioners and threatening them to
settle the dispute by paying amount to the 6th respondent and handover the
business to the respondents no.5 and 6 immediately, as illegal, arbitrary,
violative of Arts 21 of the Constitution of India and misuse of powers vested
with the office of 4th respondents and consequently desist the 4th respondent
from calling petitioners to the police station and threatening them to settle the
dispute by paying amount to the 6th respondent and handover the business
to the respondents no. 5 and 6 and pass

sentences.text:
3. When the matter is taken up for hearing, Sri P.Ajay Babu, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home, would submit that based on the contents of the complaint made by the 4th respondent,
the police registered a case in Crime No.241 of 2024 dated 02.07.2024 for the offence punishable under Section 420, 406 IPC against the petitioners herein.
Therefore, police are calling the petitioners only for enquiry purpose in the above case.
Except for the purpose of the said case, the police are not interfering with the civil disputes between the petitioners and the unofficial respondents.
4. Considering the submissions, the writ petition is disposed of.
However, police are directed to follow due process of law regarding the crime which is registered against the petitioners.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel thereto, miscellaneous petitions pending if any, shall stand closed.
